# Header overflow repartition publishes no settle signal to the DOM

## Context

The fourth seam of #18151, measured 2026-09-03 (issuecomment-5527971880) on a downstream pointer-driven e2e suite at engine `ae9640376f`. `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow#applySplit` (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:808`) marks overflowing header buttons `vdom.removeDom = true` (:895) and calls `owner.update()` (:902), so a header action that is visible, enabled and rect-stable can be detached before a click dispatches. The engine knows exactly when the repartition is idle — `whenProjectionIdle()` (:515) resolves the `projectionIdleWaiters` (:240, :505–508) once the measuring latch releases and the coalesced rerun has settled — and nothing publishes that to the DOM.

The dock already solved the same problem for motion: `projection/MotionSignal.mjs` keeps `neo-dashboard-dock-animating` on the workspace component while any motion is in flight — counted, instance-keyed, fail-safe — and `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:5` documents it as the observable motion lifecycle. The header repartition is a second mechanism with no signal.

Measured consumer cost: three sites failed as three different lies — a bare 2-minute `beforeEach` timeout, a bare 4-minute timeout, and a `waitForEvent "page"` 45 s timeout that reads as a tear-out vessel defect. A consumer-side bounded click plus a two-sample rect-stability wait moved 6/8 → 7/8 green at n=8, which is not a fix: `element is not stable` (motion, waitable) and `element was detached from the DOM` with the node stable (a replacement, unpredictable from outside) are two failure modes, and retrying is unsafe because half the targets are toggles.

## The Problem

A consumer polls rectangles to approximate a boolean the engine holds. Every engine dock spec drives operations through the Neural Link and none clicks a header action with a pointer, so the gap is invisible from inside — the same structure as the epic's other seams. The worker-side promise has one consumer (`src/draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:147`), no Neural Link surface exposes it, and the DOM carries nothing.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` is a GENERIC tab plugin (`Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow`, attaching to `Neo.tab.header.Toolbar`). It imports no dock module and must not start; it fires no events today.
- The dock installs it in `projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1253` (`{module: TabOverflowPlugin, projectAsAction: true}`) inside the tab header toolbar config the adapter builds with the workspace in its projection context; the Reconciler reaches the plugin through `getPlugin('tab-overflow')` (:414, :575, :731).
- `MotionSignal`: static `enter(component)` / `leave(component)`, counted per instance, `FAIL_SAFE_MS = 2000`, `SIGNAL_CLS = 'neo-dashboard-dock-animating'`. Producers today: the Workspace FLIP commit (`Workspace.mjs:3009/:3018`), `RevealOverlay` (:239/:250), `plugin/Maximize` (:471/:480), `TabEnterButton` (:139/:150). Its docblock's reason to exist is one lifecycle to observe no matter how many mechanisms animate; the `observe_motion` e2e specs key off the class.
- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` is under the standing stop-adding directive (PR #18213): the subscription does not land there.

## The Fix

Generic producer first, dock consumer second:

1. **`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`** publishes the repartition lifecycle as events on its owner toolbar — `overflowProjectionStart` when the measuring latch arms and `overflowProjectionIdle` when the idle waiters resolve, exactly the two moments `whenProjectionIdle()` already brackets. No class, no dock import; `whenProjectionIdle()` unchanged.
2. **`projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs`**: the toolbar config built at :1253 gains listeners for the two events that route into `MotionSignal.enter(toolbar)` / `MotionSignal.leave(toolbar)` — the header toolbar itself is the carrier, the producer's own component, as `TabEnterButton` already does. *(Amended 2026-09-05 from "on the workspace": toggling the class on the workspace root from inside a header pass forces a whole-tree vnode sync while that header's buttons are being replaced; at boot on the `dock-maximize` fixture that sync failed on a retired button id and stranded the projection — the root is not a safe carrier for a producer that replaces nodes under it.)* Counted: a repartition nested in a motion on the same toolbar holds until the last producer leaves. Fail-safe: a lost idle clears within `FAIL_SAFE_MS`. Instance-keyed: a re-projected header cannot decrement a predecessor's entry. A consumer waits for the class to be absent from the dock host's subtree, for motion and repartition alike.
3. **Docs**: the `MotionSignal` docblock and `Container.scss:5` name the repartition as the second producer class.

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029 — presentation tier only (the JSON-first guardrail): no persisted shape, no operation, no Neural Link tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] While an overflow repartition is in flight on a projected tab header of a dock workspace, that header toolbar carries `neo-dashboard-dock-animating`; it leaves when the repartition and any concurrent producer on the toolbar have settled, so a consumer finds the class absent from the dock host's subtree only when every header is idle. *(Amended 2026-09-05: carrier = the header toolbar, not the workspace root — see The Fix.)* Unit: two headers repartitioning concurrently each hold their class until idle; a nested producer on one toolbar holds it until the last leaves; red on `dev`.
- [ ] `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` imports no dock module (its import list is unchanged) and publishes start/idle as owner events; `whenProjectionIdle()` and the header `SortZone` consumer keep their behaviour (existing arms green).
- [ ] A measure pass that throws cannot wedge the signal: the plugin's latch releases (existing contract) and the signal clears through `MotionSignal`'s fail-safe within `FAIL_SAFE_MS`. Unit with an injected throwing `getDomRect` and injected timers.
- [ ] A re-projected header — a new plugin instance under the same ids — can neither strand a predecessor's entry nor strip a live one; the instance-keyed contract holds through one dock re-projection. Unit.
- [ ] Component tier (`component/dashboard`, real browser): a focus-driven repartition sets the class and clears it, and a pointer click on a header action gated on the class leaving lands on the intended, attached node. Red-first control: on `dev` the class never appears during the repartition.
- [ ] `MotionSignal`'s docblock and `Container.scss` name the repartition producer; no new tool, no new persisted state.

## Out of Scope

A DOM class on non-dock tab containers (events only there; a follow-up if a consumer asks); the overflow partition algorithm; new Neural Link tools; the consumer's own click bounding.

## Avoided Traps

- **Toggling a class inside `applySplit`.** Uncounted, without a fail-safe, keyed by id — the class `MotionSignal` exists to replace. Route through the owner.
- **A second class (`neo-dashboard-dock-projecting`).** Consumers would wait on two; "do not click yet" is one question.
- **Importing `MotionSignal` into `src/tab`.** The generic plugin would depend on the dock projection tier.
- **Landing the subscription in `Workspace.mjs`.** The stop-adding directive; the adapter already owns the toolbar config and the workspace context.
- **Reading the rect-stability workaround as the fix.** 7/8 at n=8 is a coin's width from luck, and the replacement failure mode is unwaitable from outside.
- **An arm that asserts the event fired or the class was added while nothing repartitions** (the #18134 trap). The component arm asserts the click's target and the class's absence on `dev`.
